name: Comoros

findings.summary: Huawei is contractor for Comores Télécom's network modernisation and fixed-mobile convergence project, funded by a 2018 China Eximbank concessional loan; the operator migrated to the new Huawei system in July 2020 and launched Nafassi FTTH in 2022.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor Huawei, so prc. Tier 5 because La Gazette reports the operator's migration to the FMC system completed (with Huawei optimising post-migration bugs) and AidData records FTTH service launched 22 March 2022; AidData still lists the project as in implementation, so a reviewer may prefer tier 4. US$85.8m is the loan face value per World Bank DRS via AidData; the Huawei commercial contract is about US$81m (2017).

findings.builder: Hengtong Marine Cable System; Huawei Marine Networks
findings.summary: Phase 1 of the national fibre backbone, China Eximbank-financed from 2010, delivered the 260 km Avassa inter-island submarine cable and the FLY-LION3 Mayotte–Anjouan link, built by Huawei Marine and Hengtong for Comores Télécom; completed January 2017.
findings.analyst_inference: Cable/equipment vendor Huawei Marine (now HMN Tech), so prc. Loan signed December 2010; US$31.76m is AidData's face-value conversion of RMB 215m. Pre-2020 by completion date; current operation not confirmed by this run, though nothing suggests decommissioning. Comores Télécom reportedly also owns other cables on the same route.

findings.summary: A Huawei release on a 2018 presidential visit says Huawei, present since 2005, helped build Comoros' 2G, 3G and 4G networks and claims its products serve about 80% of the population.
findings.analyst_inference: S4 corporate release: evidence the claim was made, not that it is true. Operators unnamed; likely overlaps COM-001 for Comores Télécom. The radio vendor of the second operator, Yas Comores (AXIAN, ex-Telma), was not established. Pre-2020 and not confirmed current.

findings.controller: Government of the Union of the Comoros
findings.local_actor: Government of the Union of the Comoros
findings.financier: African Development Bank (AfDF and Transition Support Facility grants, about EUR 9.51m for the wider digitisation project)
findings.summary: AfDB approved about EUR 9.5m in grants for digitising the Comorian economy, including a new government data centre and operationalising the existing secondary data centre, with a private firm to run them under a PPP.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner presumed to be the state (not stated explicitly), so domestic; builder, equipment vendor and PPP operator not named. Tier 2 because the data centre is planned with grant financing approved but no build contract found; a reviewer could argue tier 4 for financing closed. Grant value covers the whole digitisation project, so no value assigned to the facility. A foreign PPP operator could change the pole.

research_gaps: Radio/core and 5G vendor of Yas Comores (AXIAN; 5G launched Moroni 2025, IFC EUR 25m loan June 2025) not named in the operator release or Ecofin.
Who will build, equip and operate (PPP) the AfDB-funded government data centre, and has construction started?
Is the Huawei FMC/modernisation project (AidData 87222) formally complete, and are Avassa and FLY-LION3 still in service?
Any Comores Télécom privatisation or new cable (e.g. 2Africa landing) that could shift network control.
